Actually I disagree. I believe she would have been a legend then as she is now, because that is a part of who you are, not what you do. And it's who she is that you have to look to for clues on what her life would have been like then, not what she does. What you do is just a hat you wear while it suits the times. but who you are is harder to just pick up or shrug off.

So what is it about Cadsuane I think would have been of value in the 2nd age? Well you said it yourself - "Also, her specialty has been the gentling of channeling men '''and keeping them alive'''." 
Finding them and gentling them was something useful to do that her skills lent themselves toward, given the times she lived in. Nothing special there. But the fact that she devoted so much more of her efforts outside of what anyone would have expected of her to make sure they '''stayed''' alive shows a level of service to her fellow man that would have been respected in the 2nd age. She would have had to express that trait in some other way, but the traits that the 2nd age respected are a part of who she is.

However, what I find sad is that the traits to have ended up serving the Shadow in the 2nd age are also in her. As Tam noted, to achieve her goals, she's not above being a base bully for one thing. 
But more important is her inner monologue when she is trying to figure out how to break Semirhage. She realizes that what would break the archetypical sadist was the same thing that would break her, destroying her pride. Cadsuane is full of pride and THAT's the one thing shared by all the forsaken. In a time when the suppression of ego in favor of serving your fellow man was 'supposed' to be the status quo, the forsaken were the exceptions to the rule. Each of them was so full of pride in their own self importance that they eventually lost perspective on their own value with respect to their fellow citizens. when you start thinking you're more valuable than those around you to the point that even your frivolous desires outweigh the human rights of others, you're on a one way ticket to evils-ville.

So long story short (too late), I think Cadsuane has what it takes inside to be legendary in any age. But ironically, I think it was living in an age of hardship and constant battle against the Shadow, that kept her in the Light.
